colour.description: Its flight plan's item 19 A/, its colour and markings

dueItems.description: What else falls due on it as its owner keeps it: ADs (14 CFR 91.417(a)(2)(v)) and other items

equipment.description: Its flight plan's item 10a, its navigation, communication and approach equipment (AIM Appendix 4, TBL 4-2)

figures.description: Its own handbook figures as its pilot gave them; each null where not given

handbook.description: Its handbook figures as its pilot confirmed them from a photographed page: the engine contract's HandbookFigures, in the app's units; null until then

inspections.description: Its inspections and tests, as recorded, each with the last day it is good for

openSquawks.description: Its squawks not yet fixed, newest first

surveillance.description: Its flight plan's item 10b, its surveillance equipment (AIM Appendix 4, TBL 4-3)

vorCheck.description: Its last VOR check for IFR (14 CFR 91.171): when, how, where, the bearing error, and the last day it is good for -- 30 days on, if the error was within the check's limit

figures.description: Its own handbook figures, all at once (null in it clears one); left out, they stay as they were

access.description: SIGN_IN: a session can be had, and the developer's workspace needs the role. OPEN: nobody can sign in and everything is open (the local stack). CLOSED: nobody can sign in, and writes and the developer's workspace are refused.

claudeFeatures.description: Who has the features Claude writes (the assistant, the written briefing, the readings in words, checkpoint descriptions, the mock oral, a photographed page read): OFF, the default, for nobody, whatever else is sold or open -- the apps then use only on-device models and the engine's own words; DEVELOPERS; or EVERYONE signed in.

providers.description: The OIDC providers with real credentials, by registration id: the sign-in buttons to offer. Empty where only the emailed link signs in (the local stack).

subscriptions.description: Whether this deployment sells the subscription; where not, the page says nothing of one.

Corner.description: A corner of the CG envelope: arm aft of the datum and weight

Cruise.description: A cruise performance table's row: pressure altitude, power, RPM, true airspeed, fuel burn

approachesInWindow.description: Approaches logged in the 6 calendar months before this one

instrumentCurrentFrom.description: The first day of an instrument currency not begun yet: approaches flown this month count from the first of next month (14 CFR 61.57(c)(1)), and until then the pilot is not current; null when current now

instrumentCurrentUntil.description: The last day of instrument currency (14 CFR 61.57(c)(1), or 61.57(d)'s check); in the past where it has lapsed, null where none is logged

ipcNeededAfter.description: The day after which only an instrument proficiency check restores it (61.57(d))

ipcOn.description: The last instrument proficiency check, as the pilot gives it

trackingInWindow.description: Intercepting and tracking courses logged in them

Distance.description: A takeoff or landing distance table's row: ground roll and total over a 50 ft obstacle

DueDto.description: One thing that falls due: the pilot's currency, an airplane's inspection, or an item its owner keeps

daysLeft.description: Days from today to dueOn: 0 today, below 0 past

dueAtHours.description: The time in service it is due at

dueOn.description: The last day it is good for, or the day it is due

hoursLeft.description: Hours from the time in service now, where the owner gave it

itemId.description: The due item's, for an owner's item

rule.description: The rule that asks for it, or an AD's number

what.description: What it is, as a key: flight-review, medical, day-passengers, night-passengers, instrument; annual, hundred-hour, elt, elt-battery, static, transponder, vor-check; item

dueAtHours.description: The time in service the next action is required at, if by hours

dueOn.description: The day the next action is required, if by day

reference.description: An AD's number and revision date, or the item's own reference

FeatureUse.description: One paid feature's uses this month (UTC)

FlightPlanFilingRequest.description: A flight plan, FAA Form 7233-4's items

departureTime.description: The departure time, an instant (item 13, UTC)

HandbookFigures.description: An airplane's handbook figures in the app's units (the engine contract's HandbookFigures)

InspectionsDto.description: An airplane's inspections and tests as recorded, each with the last day it is good for: the annual to the end of the 12th calendar month after (14 CFR 91.409(a)), the altimeter and static test and the transponder test to the end of the 24th (91.411(a), 91.413(a)), the ELT's inspection to the end of the 12th (91.207(d)); the 100-hour due at 100 hours of time in service after the last (91.409(b)). Null where not recorded

eltBatteryDueOn.description: The date the ELT's battery is to be replaced by, as marked on it (91.207(c))

forHire.description: Whether it carries people or is given for flight instruction for hire, when the 100-hour inspection applies (91.409(b))

OwnFigures.description: An airplane's own performance figures from its handbook; each null where not given

climbRateFpm.description: Its best rate of climb at sea level, fpm

emptyMomentLbIn.description: Its basic empty moment, lb-in, from its weight and balance record

emptyWeightLb.description: Its basic empty weight, lb, from its weight and balance record

glideRatio.description: Its still-air glide ratio, propeller windmilling, flaps up (its handbook's Section 3)

serviceCeilingFt.description: Its service ceiling, ft (the altitude where its best climb is 100 fpm)

taxiFuelGal.description: Its fuel for engine start, taxi and takeoff, gal

today.description: The day the days left are counted from

developer.description: Whether this pilot also does development work here: the training workspace and the developer console are theirs, a plain pilot's are not.

email.description: Email address from the identity provider

fullName.description: Their name as their certificate gives it: the pilot in command a flight plan names (item 19 C/) and an endorsement names them by

homeBase.description: Their airplane's home base, an airport identifier

phone.description: Their telephone number, the contact a flight plan's item 19 C/ asks for

SubscriptionDto.description: The signed-in pilot's subscription to the paid features

entitled.description: Whether the paid features are theirs now

plan.description: MONTHLY or YEARLY, when paid for

state.description: FREE (none), TRIAL (the free month), SUBSCRIBED (paid for), or COMPED (given: a developer's, an instructor's)

store.description: Where it was bought, when paid for

trialAvailable.description: Whether the free month is still theirs to start: once an account

until.description: When the free month or the paid time runs out; null for FREE and COMPED

uses.description: This month's uses of each paid feature Claude writes, against its cap

VorCheckDto.description: A VOR check for IFR (14 CFR 91.171)

goodThrough.description: The last day it is good for: 30 days on (91.171(a)(2))

limitDeg.description: The largest error 91.171 allows for this kind of check, degrees

info.description: Scores candidate checkpoints and dead-reckoning nav-log data for a VFR route. See /swagger-ui/index.html for the interactive docs.
info.title: Wingtip Maps API

post.description: Checks the native sheet's identity token (Apple's keys, issuer, this app's bundle id, and its nonce where one is sent) and signs the pilot in on this session. 404 where no iOS app is set up.

200.description: Signed in; `next` is where to go

401.description: Not a token Apple issued to this app, or no verified email

404.description: No iOS app set up here

post.summary: Sign in with Apple from the iOS app

post.description: Kept by this session, used once. Give Apple its SHA-256 as lowercase hex (ASAuthorizationAppleIDRequest.nonce), then send it as `nonce` with the identity token.
post.summary: A nonce for Sign in with Apple from the iOS app

get.summary: Whether anyone can sign in here

post.description: The TV shows `userCode` and the address `verificationPath` on this site, and asks /api/auth/device/token with `deviceCode` every `interval` seconds until a pilot signed in on a phone types the code in. 429 past twenty an hour from one place.

429.description: Too many codes asked for from here

post.summary: A code for a TV to sign in with

post.description: From the phone, signed in. 404 for a code no TV is showing now (mistyped, used or ten minutes old); 429 past ten tries in ten minutes.

204.description: The TV will be signed in at its next ask

401.description: Not signed in on this phone

404.description: No TV is showing that code now

post.summary: Sign in the TV showing this code as the pilot signed in here

post.description: 202 while not yet; 200 once it has, the TV then signed in on this session, the code spent; 410 for a code ten minutes old or unknown, for which the TV asks for a new one.

200.description: Signed in; `next` is where to go

202.description: Not yet; ask again in `interval` seconds

410.description: The code is spent, too old or unknown

post.summary: The TV asking whether its code has been typed in

post.description: Always 202 -- the response never reveals whether the address has signed in before.

429.description: Too many asks from this address this hour

post.description: 302 into the app, now signed in -- a developer to dev mode, anyone else to the planner -- on success; 400 for an expired, already-used or unrecognized token.
post.summary: Sign in from a magic link

delete.description: The pilot and everything that was theirs -- aircraft, flights with their nav logs and tracks, logbook, endorsements, their own checkpoint notes, the sign-in links sent to them -- and every session they hold. Nothing is deleted when the planner cannot take the notes (502).

502.description: Nothing deleted: the planner could not take the notes

get.description: Creates the pilot record on first sign-in. 204, with nothing, when no one is signed in: the ordinary answer for a signed-out page, not a refusal.

put.description: What a flight plan's item 19 C/ asks with the pilot in command's name (AIM Appendix 4), both at once; blank is none. Their name is set with PUT /api/training/name.

400.description: Not a telephone number, or not an airport identifier

put.summary: The signed-in pilot's telephone number and home base

get.description: The account, airplanes and squawks, flights with nav logs, tracks, share links and watches, logbook, currency, training and instructing, each as its own endpoint answers it; the pilot's own checkpoint notes, reminders, subscription, paid-feature counts and connected AI apps (never a token); sent as a download.
get.summary: Everything kept for the signed-in pilot, as one JSON file
